kinds.AMBIGUOUS: Could serve more than one canonical term. Deliberately not mapped.
kinds.COMPOUND: One cell naming several areas at once. Parts are recorded; the cell is NOT split into independent rows.
kinds.CROSS_SLOT_PACKED: One value packing a group and an area into one field. Both halves are declared terms in different slots; the value is reported, not split, because splitting changes the row's cardinality.
kinds.DECLARED_JUDGMENT: Different words, judged equivalent by this package. A reviewer may disagree; the original term is always retained.
kinds.EXACT_VARIANT: Same words, different case, spacing or separator. Mechanical; safe to accept.
kinds.GRANULARITY_MISMATCH: The term is finer-grained than the canonical. Mapped to its parent, but rows are NOT interchangeable with parent rows.
kinds.SCOPE_VALUE: A legitimate value that is not one of the three groups - it describes scope, not a mis-spelling.
kinds.SCOPE_VALUE_AREA: A legitimate value naming every area rather than one. Not a mis-spelling; must not be joined as a single area.
kinds.UNRESOLVED_CONCEPT: Names a concept this package will not equate with any canonical term. Needs the owning lane to decide.

patterns.finding: These terms use a different taxonomy, not a different spelling of the same one. They name concepts outside the four assessment areas entirely - data classification, records handling, accessibility, procurement, governance - so no canonical assessment area applies.
patterns.question: Is this column the four-area assessment taxonomy under other names, or a separate policy-topic taxonomy that should not be joined to it at all?
patterns.why_not_split: " / " does not carry one meaning in this column. In "Deployment / operations" it joins two words of a single concept; in "Access / IAM / software delivery" it appears to join separate concepts. Splitting on it would invent an "Access" area and destroy "Deployment and operations". This package does not split on an ambiguous separator.
